To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conduction band offset of the cubic Si3N4/cubic GaN interface is 1.17 ± 0.02 eV, that the interface trap density is 2.4 × 1011 eV−1 cm−2, and that the conductivity of the MIS structure grown with the highest substrate temperature is minimized.
the interface state density of the cubic GaN/Si3N4 MIS structures is low, and that the conduction band offset between cubic GaN and Si3N4, determined by flatband voltage measurements, is 1.17 eV.
we report the first MIS devices on cubic GaN grown by MBE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of cubic GaN MIS structures with a Si3N4 gate insulator.
the electrical characterization of MIS structures with cubic GaN as semiconductor and Si3N4as dielectric.
the electrical characterization of MIS structures based on cubic GaN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interface state density of cubic GaN is comparable to that of hexagonal GaN.
the interface trap density of our in situ grown cubic GaN MIS structures is low and comparable to the interface state density of the best reported hexagonal GaN MIS devices.
our MIS structure grown at a substrate temperature of 600 °C shows the lowest interface trap charge density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to grow high-quality cubic GaN on 3C-SiC (0 00 1) substrated by MBE.
the Si3N4 cubic GaN MIS structure grown at a substrate temperature of 600 °C has a low interface trapped charge density, which can be used to fabricate high-quality MISFETs.
the MIS structure grown on 3 C–SiC substrate at 600 ° C has the highest insulating quality and the lowest density of interface states.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interface trap density in our cubic GaN/Si3N4 system is comparable to or even lower than the one reported for hexagonal MIS devices, which is a promising step towards high-quality cubic GaN MIS structures for future electronic and optoelectronic devices.
the interface trap density of our MIS structures is very low, which makes these structures promising candidates for the fabrication of cubic GaN-based electronic devices.
Si3N4 cubic GaN MIS structure can be grown in situ by MBE and the interface trap density is very low.
